    3D sky

    Live aircraft heard by this receiver. Changes take effect straight away and are remembered on this screen.

    Press Enter or Find to search the airports on this page by code, name or city.
    My places
    Type an address or a city, or paste a latitude and longitude from Google Maps. Each place gets a label on the ground and joins the list above.
    Your places stay on this device. They are never sent to this site or saved on it. Only a rough position, to about seven miles, is used to ask for the aircraft and the weather there. With the box unticked, your places are forgotten when you close this page.
    Type a flight number such as DL1234 or a tail number such as N123AB. Beyond the antenna's reach its position comes from ADSB.lol. Its caption says where it is, in nautical miles from the nearest places, from a list of places by GeoNames carried in this page.
    Up to 10 tail numbers or flight numbers. You get an alert when the antenna hears one. Alerts come only while this page is open.
    Taking over is flying with the mouse, the wheel or the arrow keys, clicking or double-clicking an aircraft, or picking one in search. The wait counts from the last time you touched the controls. A starts the tour again at any time.
    Day, night, dawn and dusk come from this computer's clock and the sunrise and sunset for the place on screen.
    The real weather is for the place on screen. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com. The other choices are for trying each look.
    Shown at dusk, at night and at dawn on aircraft below 5,000 feet.
    Private aircraft and airlines the sky does not know. Airline and military paint is never replaced.
